fact: The UN in Lesotho says the Government, led by the Ministry of Gender, Youth and Social Development with EU, UNICEF and World Bank support, is transitioning Child Grants Programme payments from third-party cash-in-transit to mobile payments through selected mobile network providers.

The EU/UNICEF-backed Ntlafatsa Bana project (2023-2026) aims to improve Child Grants Programme delivery by shifting towards digital payments and digitalising payments to beneficiaries, and the Ministry of Gender, Youth and Social Development is transitioning to digital payments.
UNICEF says that through the Ntlafatsa Bana programme 25,575 households now receive Child Grants Programme payments through digital mobile cash transfers.
The Lesotho Times reports that more than 40,000 elderly people, about 53 percent of all old-age pension beneficiaries, now receive their grants electronically, mostly through M-Pesa and EcoCash.

Lesotho News Agency reports that 23 of 30 cash pay-points for the elderly pension grant in Quthing district have closed after more than 4,800 beneficiaries were enrolled on mobile money (M-Pesa and EcoCash) since September 2024, with over 1,000 still paid in cash.
